summary: Proxy Mobile IPv6 requires mobile access gateways to use a fixed link-local and link-layer address on shared links, so a node sees no change when it roams. This RFC reserves an IPv6 interface identifier for that purpose.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC reserves specific link-layer and IPv6 identifiers for Proxy Mobile IPv6 gateways. The shared values help mobile nodes see a consistent network attachment when moving between gateways.

subtitle: Reserved Ethernet and IPv6 identifiers for Proxy Mobile IPv6 access gateways.

tldr.problem: Proxy Mobile IPv6 requires fixed gateway link-local and link-layer addresses but had not reserved specific values for them.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC reserves Ethernet address 00-00-5E-00-52-13 and IPv6 interface identifier 0200:5EFF:FE00:5213 for shared access links.
tldr.outcome: Gateways SHOULD use the reserved values; the RFC notes that shared fixed addresses raise ownership concerns across domains.

today: RFC 6543 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 5213. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes it.

sections.title: The Fixed-Address Requirement
sections.content:
Proxy Mobile IPv6 lets a network provide mobility support without requiring the mobile node to take part in mobility signaling. RFC 5213 requires gateways in a domain to use fixed link-local and link-layer addresses on access links shared with mobile nodes.

The base specification did not reserve values for those addresses, creating an operational challenge across equipment from different vendors.
sections.plainLanguage: To keep the mobile node's network view stable, gateways need to use consistent addresses. This RFC chooses values for them.

sections.title: The Reserved Addresses
sections.content:
The RFC reserves Ethernet unicast address 00-00-5E-00-52-13. Mobile access gateways SHOULD use it on all access links shared with mobile nodes.

It also reserves IPv6 interface identifier 0200:5EFF:FE00:5213, a modified EUI-64 identifier generated from that Ethernet address. Gateways SHOULD use the resulting link-local address in Neighbor Discovery communication with mobile nodes.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC reserves one Ethernet address and an IPv6 interface identifier derived from it. Gateways should use these values on the shared links.

sections.title: Registry and Security Considerations
sections.content:
IANA recorded the Ethernet address in its unicast-use registry and the interface identifier in the Reserved IPv6 Interface Identifiers registry.

The RFC notes that the same address values are now used beyond one Proxy Mobile IPv6 domain. This expands an existing address-ownership concern to a multi-domain environment, and future work may be needed.
sections.plainLanguage: The values are recorded in IANA registries. Because multiple domains may use the same values, proving ownership can be more complicated.
